title: Squarefree Sumsets
description: For an infinite A ⊆ ℕ with every a+b squarefree, how fast must A grow? Erdős conjectured exponential growth is necessary. van Doorn–Tao (2025) proved bounds: a_j > 0.24·j^{4/3} and a_j < exp(5j/log j).

overview.historicalContext: Erdős posed this problem in the context of understanding how multiplicative constraints (squarefreeness) restrict additive structure (sumsets). A number n is squarefree if no prime square p² divides it — equivalently, its prime factorization has all exponents ≤ 1. The density of squarefree numbers is 6/π² ≈ 0.608, but requiring ALL pairwise sums to be squarefree is extremely restrictive. Van Doorn and Tao (2025) made significant progress, proving a polynomial lower bound a_j > 0.24·j^{4/3} and constructing sequences achieving subexponential growth a_j < exp(5j/log j). Konyagin provided complementary finite-set bounds: |A ∩ [1,N]| ≤ C·N^{11/15}. The central question — whether exponential growth is truly necessary — remains open.
overview.problemStatement: Let A be an infinite set of positive integers such that a + b is squarefree for all a, b ∈ A. Must A grow at least exponentially?
overview.proofStrategy: We define SquarefreeSumset as the condition that all pairwise sums are squarefree, axiomatize an increasing enumeration enumSet, and state the conjecture as exponential lower bound on enumSet. Known bounds by van Doorn–Tao and Konyagin are stated as axioms. Basic properties (empty set, subsets, singletons) are proved.
keyInsights: The squarefree sumset condition links additive combinatorics to multiplicative number theory: a + b must avoid all p² for every pair, creating a global constraint from local divisibility conditions
Van Doorn–Tao's polynomial lower bound a_j > 0.24·j^{4/3} rules out slow polynomial growth but leaves a wide gap to the conjectured exponential growth
The upper bound exp(5j/log j) is subexponential — such sequences exist, so exponential growth is not the only option. The question is whether true exponential growth (C^j for C > 1) is unavoidable

Konyagin's finite-set bound |A| ≤ C·N^{11/15} connects to sieve methods: the exponent 11/15 comes from bounding the number of integers in [1,N] avoiding squares in their sumset via large sieve techniques

The formalization axiomatizes enumSet as a strictly monotone surjection onto A — this is the standard way to discuss growth rates of infinite sets in Lean, avoiding constructive issues with well-ordering

sections.title: Introduction and Known Results
sections.summary: Module documentation: states Erdős Problem 1103 on squarefree sumsets, known results by van Doorn–Tao (upper/lower bounds) and Konyagin (finite case), and reference to erdosproblems.com.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines SquarefreeSumset A as ∀ a b ∈ A, Squarefree(a+b). Axiomatizes enumSet as a strictly monotone function with range equal to A, providing an increasing enumeration.

sections.title: Main Conjecture
sections.summary: ErdosProblem1103: for every infinite A with SquarefreeSumset, ∃ C > 1 such that eventually C^j ≤ a_j. Uses Filter.atTop for the 'eventually' quantifier.

sections.title: Known Bounds
sections.summary: Three axiomatized results: (1) van Doorn–Tao upper bound — existence of sequence with a_j < exp(5j/log j), (2) van Doorn–Tao lower bound — a_j > 0.24·j^{4/3} for all squarefree-sumset sequences, (3) Konyagin finite bound — |A ∩ [1,N]| ≤ C·N^{11/15}.

sections.title: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Four basic results: singleton characterization (SquarefreeSumset {a} ↔ Squarefree(2a)), empty set is trivially squarefree-sumset, subset monotonicity, and 1 is squarefree. Two proved, two axiomatized.

conclusion.summary: The formalization captures Erdős Problem 1103 on squarefree sumsets with the main conjecture and known bounds by van Doorn–Tao and Konyagin. All 0 sorries — the open conjecture is stated as a definition (Prop), and deep results are axiomatized.
conclusion.implications: Resolving whether exponential growth is necessary would illuminate the fundamental interaction between additive structure and multiplicative constraints in number theory, with connections to sieve methods, the distribution of squarefree numbers, and the geometry of numbers.
openQuestions: Is exponential growth necessary for infinite squarefree-sumset sequences, or can subexponential constructions like exp(j/log j) be improved to polynomial?
Can the polynomial lower bound j^{4/3} be improved toward exponential via refined sieve estimates?
What is the exact growth threshold — is there a sharp transition between possible and impossible growth rates?
